column1: # scripts/check_invariant_stop_sites.py counts the calls in maintained kernel/
# Takibi code (comments blanked, kernel/tests excluded) and fails on a
# function with no row, a count over or UNDER its rows, an unknown class, or
# a ladder row without an issue. Rows of one function may split its sites
# across classes; their counts add up. Lowering or removing a row is the edit
# a retired stop makes; adding or raising one is a decision about a new stop
# and is made by hand with its class and reason written here.
# Classes (the rule a stop is admitted under):
#   frame       the stop runs at a frame site (#1017): exception entry/return
#               or the assembly stack handoff, where no Takibi caller exists
#               to take a value and the saved frame is the only report.
#   unmodelled  the stop guards a premise no model or type covers: a hardware
#               or firmware fact, a boot layout fact, a device's answer.
#   ladder      a candidate to move up the ladder: the premise could be a
#               compile-time rule (rung 1) or is already stated by a model
#               (rung 2) whose conformance the stop only spot-checks. The
#               issue column names where the move is tracked; "unfiled:" is
#               not accepted, so the coordinator files it first.
# value: "handler" when the function already returns a fallible value on the
# stop's path (rule 2 candidate: the stop could become that value), "-" else.
# Columns: file, function, class, count, value, issue, reason (tab separated).
